result:
`final.py` scores **78.4×** on the search split (the baseline is about 1.0). I used **5 of the 24 scorer calls**, one of which the scorer rejected.

I said I'd spend about 15 minutes but stopped after about 5. The last three variants I measured on my local test harness were no faster, so I didn't spend the rest of the time or calls. The hidden-instance score is still unknown. The only held-out check I ran was on my own harness, on test seeds I never tuned on.

| | search score | candidate CPU |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | ~1.0 | 1.33 s (the reference) |
| first working version (`c1`) | 67.4× | 19.7 ms |
| **final (`c6` → `final.py`)** | **78.4×** | **16.9 ms** |

**Why it's faster:** the reference compares every pair of records, about 4.5M comparisons. The final version only compares records that can possibly reach 80 %:
- **Shared rare word:** words are ranked from rarest to most common across the whole input. A record can only be within 80 % of another if they share a word among the first `len − ⌈0.8·len⌉ + 1` words of their ranked lists. Records are indexed by those words only, and only records that meet that way get compared.
- **Size limit:** a record is never compared with one smaller than 80 % of its size.
- **Exact duplicates:** records with the same word set are grouped first and reported as pairs directly. Sets of 3 or fewer words can only match an identical set, so the search skips them.
- **One-off words:** if a record's ranked prefix contains only words that appear in no other record, it can't pair with anything and is skipped.
- Each surviving candidate is checked with the exact rule from the docstring, `9·|A∩B| ≥ 4·(|A|+|B|)`, which is the same as `5·|A∩B| ≥ 4·|A∪B|`.

**Checks:** my local test harness compares the output against the reference on 311 small edge cases: empty records, whitespace-only records, case differences, repeated words and boundary sizes. It also covers two 3,000-record inputs and 30 extra randomized inputs. Every pair matched, with no duplicates and `i < j` throughout.

**Candidate log** (calls left: 19):

| candidate | change | harness | scorer | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| c1 | shared-rare-word index + size limit | 16.6 ms | 67.4× | first working version |
| c2 / c3 | group exact duplicates, `Counter`, word ranks as integers | 12.7 ms | – | kept |
| c4 | alphabetical word order instead of rarity | 312 ms | – | dropped (far too many candidates) |
| c5 | prune words that appear only once | 13.1 ms | 72.6× | kept |
| c6 | skip sets of ≤3 words | 12.7 ms | **78.4×** | **final** |
| c7 | build duplicate groups with built-in calls | 13.0 ms | – | dropped |
| c8 | import from `_collections` to cut import time | 12.4 ms | rejected | the scorer rejects underscore imports |
| c9 | count words in a plain loop, no `collections` | 13.1 ms | 77.8× | same within noise, dropped |
| c10 | count words on a 1-in-4 sample | 13.3 ms | – | dropped |
| c11 | build all prefixes in one comprehension | 18.7 ms* | – | dropped |

\* measured on a heavier input (longer records, larger vocabulary) that I switched the harness to after c9. On that input c6 takes 18.5 ms.

The scorer's inputs look heavier than my generator's, and on those the remaining time is mostly fixed work. Splitting records into words takes about 3 ms, and counting and sorting words takes about 5–9 ms. The comparisons themselves are now a small part.

The working files (`c1.py`–`c11.py`, `harness.py`, `bench.py`) are still in the folder.
